summary: Intermittent TLS reassembly errors and gRPC chunk drops caused by customer edge offload + DPI on private deployment
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent failures while pulling model shards and repeated gRPC stream chunk drops from serving nodes. Failures occur during large artifact downloads and during long-lived chat streaming; symptoms include repeated TLS renegotiation attempts, delayed handshake completion (200-800ms additional), and gRPC framing errors leading to 5xx retries.

Impact: Affects FinStrata internal private deployment (prod, us-east-1). Multiple model pulls and streaming sessions saw transient stalls for ~10-30s, increasing latency and causing client-side reconnects. Several retries caused elevated token cost and client errors for the customer.

Environment: Private deployment behind customer-managed edge (MPLS + SD-WAN), corporate firewall with deep-packet inspection (DPI), customer NAT appliance, TGW peering to Redwood control plane.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Trigger a large model pull for redwood/open-llama-13b-v2 via the agent on a private node behind the customer edge.
2) Stream a long-lived chat session (token window > 2048) to force multiple TCP segments and TLS records.
3) Observe occasional TLS handshake stalls, gRPC FRAME_ERROR in client logs, and partial artifact ranges failing with HTTP 499/502 on range downloads.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Client logs show repeated 'tls: short record' and 'tls: record reassembly failed' messages alongside gRPC errors: "received unexpected EOS" and "stream reset by peer".
- Serving node traces show token-generation continued but ACK gaps and retransmissions on TCP level.
- Packet captures (pcap link in comments) show segments being coalesced/large skbs leaving the host and the firewall sending truncated reassembled packets back, with TLS records split differently on egress vs. what the server expects.

Initial hypothesis: The combination of NIC offloads (GRO/GSO/TSO) on the private node and stateful DPI on the corporate edge is causing large aggregated TCP segments to be re-segmented incorrectly by the firewall, which results in TLS record boundary mismatches and reassembly errors at the Redwood side. This triggers gRPC frame parsing errors and stream resets.

Requested by customer: urgent mitigation and recommended permanent remediation; customer is on a private deployment and requires a network-compatible fix or guidance they can apply to their edge appliance.

investigation_notes: Captured and analyzed pcap from customer (s3://support-artifacts/SUP-673918/trace1.pcap). Observed egress SKBs with aggregated segments sized > 16KB (typical for enabled GSO).

Firewall shows behavior consistent with DPI that inspects and attempts to re-segment TLS records; returned segments do not preserve original TLS record boundaries causing our TLS stack to see partial records and report 'short record' or 'unexpected EOF'.
Local repro: Enabled GSO on a lab node and placed an inline proxy that performs payload inspection and segmentation. Reproduced gRPC frame errors and TLS reassembly logs matching customer trace.

Experimented with disabling GSO/GRO on the agent (via ethtool -K enp1s0g gso off gro off tso off) — after disabling, TLS reassembly errors disappeared in lab and customer reported immediate relief when they applied same change on their hosts.

Tested alternative mitigations: TCP MSS clamp at SD-WAN edge to 1200-1400 bytes prevented large SKBs from being produced and also resolved reassembly errors; however this requires config change in customer WAN (may impact throughput).
Captured server-side logs: additional handshake latency spikes correlated with packet re-ordering and retransmits; no evidence of server-side CPU resource exhaustion during incidents.
resolution:
Workaround implemented: Customer disabled NIC aggregation offloads (GSO/GRO/TSO) on private-agent hosts and applied TCP MSS clamp on SD-WAN for egress to Redwood model artifact endpoints; both actions eliminated TLS reassembly errors and gRPC frame drops.

Permanent remediation path: Customer has agreed to schedule firewall firmware update with their vendor to correct DPI re-segmentation behavior. Internally, we will add a Console alert to detect 'tls: short record' and elevated gRPC frame errors and include a KB article that documents network checks and mitigations (disable offloads, MSS clamp, vendor firmware guidance).

Rollout notes and follow-ups:
- Customer to confirm firmware patch date by 2026-03-20 and provide post-patch pcap for verification.
- INT-3245 created for Engineering to add enhanced TLS reassembly logging and an automated detection rule (assigned to runtime team).
- Support will remain in active monitoring for 72 hours post-customer firmware upgrade; set ticket to Waiting on Customer after they confirm patch scheduling.

Final status: mitigation validated in customer environment; awaiting vendor firmware update for permanent fix.
